observationsNotFindings: This is the second gate-row and register-row coexistence in the sweep and it resolves the same way the G18 pair did: four shared obligation ids, zero divergence, and each artifact naming the other and its row. Two clean instances suggest the pattern is deliberate. The standing hazard is unchanged - nothing structural prevents a future version of one from drifting from the other - so a coordinator recording either should re-check the agreement rather than assume it.

The land test is weaker here than it looks, and the artifact does not lean on it. Live DR-G20 and live DR-125 both read OPEN, so carrying the wrong row's token would have produced the correct string by coincidence. What actually distinguishes the two is stated rather than inferred: registerRowNote names DR-G20's own token and separately records that the sdk join carries DR-125's own OPEN. On the G18 pair the tokens differed and the test discriminated on its own; here it would not have.

OBL-DR125-ACTIVATION is tracked to DR-118 rather than to DR-125, which is the accurate call and easy to get wrong. The obligation's name points at DR-125 and it appears in the DR-125 join, but there at leftoverDesign false riding DR-118, and language-quality-leftover-join.v2 carries it on DR-118 itself. The artifact says 'remains on DR-118' in four places.

This join carries the corpus phrase but not the slashJoiner decomposition or the eight-surface order that the DR-125 row join carries under CLAUDE-G20CAT-V1-SF1. Nothing is lost, since the phrase contains the slash-joined set inline, but the decomposition lives on the row join and the catalog rather than here. Worth knowing which artifact to open for surface order.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. This is the second gate-row and register-row coexistence in the sweep and it resolves as the G18 pair did: four obligation ids shared with sdk-leftover-join.v4, zero divergence on either leftoverDesign or rideStanding, and each artifact naming the other and its row. The land test passes but is weaker here than it looks, and the artifact does not lean on it - live DR-G20 and live DR-125 both read OPEN, so the wrong row's token would have produced the right string by coincidence. What distinguishes them is stated: registerRowNote names DR-G20's own token and separately records that the sdk join carries DR-125's own OPEN. Both protected obligations are absent from the obligation set rather than restated, replaced by OBL-SDK-API-NOT-STOLEN riding DR-125, whose reason correctly reports that the sdk join still measures OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED leftoverDesign true - which I verified. OBL-DR125-ACTIVATION is tracked to DR-118 rather than to the row its name points at, which is the accurate call and easy to get wrong. The corpus member equals live G20 v1 and catalog v2 under == and appears in the register cell, and probing for concrete SDK surface returns nothing. One thing recorded rather than charged: this join carries the corpus phrase but not the slashJoiner decomposition the row join holds under CLAUDE-G20CAT-V1-SF1 - not required here, and the phrase carries the surfaces inline. Disclosure: the sdk-join verdict is mine, so the divergence comparison was made between obligation objects rather than verdicts. 20 attacks run, 19 refuted, 1 examined and recorded as an observation rather than a finding.
